findingsRaised.status: The CURRENT specification closes it. §5.9 (D-024, 2026-08-15) states FailureMode: FAIL_CLOSED = 0, REVIEW = 1, notes all three enums are fail-closed by construction, and warns explicitly that the Verdict numbering is the reverse of the document's prose ordering. The control snapshot has no §5.9 at all. This is direct evidence that the post-freeze amendments were doing legitimate specification work rather than supplying answers.

findingsRaised.finding: The FROZEN PROMPT does more of the deciding than the specification does, on exactly the axis these fixtures test. Its §6 pre-digests §5.2 into three pointed imperatives ('A failed rule BLOCKS. Not reviews'), and its §3 adds "'I cannot establish this' is REVIEW, not BLOCK." Six of H's nine labels rest on the first. Those restatements are faithful but considerably sharper than the spec's own prose, and every labeller gets them identically. Agreement between labellers on these fixtures is therefore weaker evidence of independent convergence than a raw disagreement rate implies — it may partly measure the prompt's steering.

The permitted specification contains a statement ABOUT THE IMPLEMENTATION: the §5.2 amendment note (D-015) says the amendment 'records the reading the implementation follows', attached to the single most label-relevant sentence in the document.

The permitted specification tells a labeller how its own output is scored. §14.9's D-011 states that a second labeller re-labels ~20%, that >10% disagreement halts Gate S2, and that John's sampling oversamples REVIEW verdicts and disagreements. A labeller who knows REVIEW draws extra scrutiny has a mild incentive to avoid REVIEW.

The harness injected the workspace CLAUDE.md and the user's persistent MEMORY.md, whose Sentinel entry describes project status, names denied paths, and states that gates are 'facilitated, never LLM-signed'. No verdict, reason code or label. THIRD labeller to report this channel unprompted (E, G, H).
